learning_outcomes.text: Students know the connections and have detailed knowledge regarding the components and functionality of modern computer systems, including the processor, memory system, and interfaces to other system components.

Based on this knowledge, students are able to evaluate computer systems and their components regarding various metrics, such as energy consumption, computing power, memory performance, etc., for their suitability for a specific task.

Furthermore, participants of this module have understood the fundamental operation and principal structure of processors at the microarchitecture level and are able to analyze the influence of architectural features, such as pipelining or out-of-order execution, on instruction execution.

syllabus_topics: Structure and function of modern processors and computer systems
Basic computer structures (Von Neumann and Harvard architecture)
Structure, classification, and technical realization of computer systems
Processing of programs by a processor
Methods for performance evaluation of processors based on standardized benchmarks
In-depth analysis of the microarchitecture level of a processor
Development and explanation of the data path and control unit
Modern methods for performance enhancement and their application areas
Various interfaces to internal and external components of the computer system
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam.
